source.title: Drik Panchang — 2026 Dwadasha Siddhividya Jayanti
notes: Drik Panchang lists twelve Siddhividya Jayantis: Saraswati, Kubjika, Siddhilakshmi, Chandika, Batuka Bhairavi, Parvati, Dakshinamurti, Gayatri, Vindhyavasini, Aparajita, Bala and Annapurna.
Dates and lunar tithis are transcribed from the retrieved Drik Panchang 2026 listing for Koath, Bihar; they are not independently recalculated for Pithoragarh.

Some dates can vary by location/sunrise convention; the same Drik listing shows Annapurna Jayanti on 24 December 2026, while other location results can show 23 December. Verify for the site's chosen location and compare with the owner's Ganesh Martand Panchang before runtime use.
This Dwadasha Siddhividya list is distinct from the separate Dashamahavidya list and must not be merged into it.

validation: Dates are transcribed from the cited Drik Panchang 2026 listing, not independently recalculated.
Do not treat this as a transcription from Lal Bahadur Shastri Panchang; it is a separate source dataset.
Before runtime use, verify each observance for Pithoragarh and compare with the project's primary Ganesh Martand Panchang.
Keep this category distinct from Dashamahavidya Jayanti data. The same deity names may have other Jayanti traditions; preserve the source's category and tithi rather than merging by name alone.

A second retrieval of the same Drik year-list rendered for Washington, D.C. shows Gayatri Jayanti on 27 August (rather than the Koath listing's 28 August), Vindhyavasini on 3 September (rather than 4 September), and Annapurna on 23 December (rather than 24 December). This demonstrates that the Koath dates must not be treated as universal.

A Pithoragarh-specific Siddhividya listing could not be reliably retrieved in this check. Do not replace dates with the Washington dates either; keep all twelve entries provisional until a location-specific listing or a reproducible local tithi/sunrise calculation is available.

Four entries now have explicitly recorded independent Drik listings for Indian cities: Saraswati (Chennai), Siddhilakshmi (Sandila), Batuka Bhairavi (Kanpur), and Vindhyavasini (Ghaziabad and Tirupati). These corroborate those dates across Indian locations but are not direct Pithoragarh results.

For the other eight observances, this pass did not obtain an independently retrievable Indian-city event page; their original Koath listing remains the only recorded date source. Do not upgrade them to locally verified.

Project decision (2026-10-16): use the Indian Drik Panchang listing as the working date set for the project; do not require a separate Pithoragarh web page for every Jayanti. Only investigate a location-specific difference if a concrete contradiction appears against the printed Ganesh Martand Panchang or the site's own tithi calculation. This is a research dataset and has not been connected to production runtime.

locationComparison.interpretation: Observed one-day differences reinforce location/sunrise sensitivity; neither listing alone establishes the correct Pithoragarh date.
